user.title: Add an Escea fireplace
user.description:
Leave the address blank to search your network for Ethernet (Generation 2) fires. For Wi-Fi (Generation 3) fires, or a fire on another network, enter its IP address.

Wi-Fi fires need **Escea NCAPI Settings** turned on in the Escea Smartheat app (Fire Settings, firmware 1.5.9 or later) and a DHCP reservation in your router.

data_description.host: Optional for Ethernet fires. Wi-Fi fires show their IP address in the Smartheat app's Wi-Fi settings page.

web.title: Fireplace web page login
web.description: The fireplace's timers, clock and diagnostics are on its web page (http://{host}). It didn't accept the usual login (serial number and PIN). Enter the login, or leave the password blank to skip: you'll still have full control, just not the timers and diagnostics.

reconfigure.title: Change the fireplace's address or web login
reconfigure.description: To add or change the web page login (for timers, the clock and diagnostics), enter it here. Usually the username is the serial number and the password is the PIN. Leave the password blank to keep the current login.

reauth_confirm.title: Fireplace web page login
reauth_confirm.description: The fireplace's web page no longer accepts the login. Usually the username is the serial number and the password is the PIN.

error.cannot_connect: The fireplace didn't answer. Check the address and that it's turned on at the wall. For a Wi-Fi fire, check that Escea NCAPI Settings is turned on in the Smartheat app.
error.no_fireplaces: No new Ethernet fires answered. Enter the IP address (Wi-Fi fires can't be found by searching).
error.port_in_use: Another program on this computer is using UDP port 3300, which fireplaces always reply to. Remove the other Escea integration, then try again.
error.invalid_auth: The web page didn't accept that login.
error.unknown: Something unexpected went wrong. The logs have the details.

abort.already_configured: This fireplace is already added. Its address has been updated.
abort.not_escea: That device isn't an Escea fireplace.
abort.wrong_fireplace: That address belongs to a different fireplace.

init.title: Options
init.description: The maximum run time turns the fire off once it has been on for that many hours. For Ethernet fires, the web page has the timers, clock and diagnostics. It can only handle the odd request, so it's read every few minutes at most.

data_description.max_run_hours: Turn the fire off after it has been on for this many hours (1 to 12). 0 turns this off. The count starts again whenever the fire is turned off and on, and after Home Assistant restarts.
data_description.web_enabled: Turn off to use control over UDP only. The timer and diagnostic entities are removed.
data_description.web_interval: Minutes between reads. Leave it at 10 unless you have a reason.

busy.message: The fireplace is still lighting or shutting down. Try again in {seconds} seconds.

invalid_state.message: The fireplace can't do that right now: {error}

mode_while_off.message: Turn the fireplace on first. Choosing Boost or Flame effect while it's off would light it. You can choose the mode straight after turning it on: it's applied once the fire has lit.

web_unavailable.message: The timers need the fireplace's web page, which isn't available. Check the web login, or turn the web page on in the integration's options.

web_login_failed.message: The fireplace's web page rejected the login.

port_in_use.message: UDP port 3300 is in use by another program.

ncapi_failed.message: The fireplace didn't accept the change: {error}

port_in_use.title: Escea Fireplace can't open UDP port 3300
port_in_use.description: Escea fireplaces always reply to UDP port 3300, so only one program on this computer can talk to them. Something else already has the port, usually Home Assistant's built-in Escea integration or the old snikch custom component. Remove the other one and restart Home Assistant.

conflict.title: Two Escea integrations are installed
conflict.description: The `{domain}` integration also talks to Escea fireplaces on UDP port 3300. Only one of them can hear the fireplaces' replies, so one will keep going unavailable. Remove `{domain}` and restart Home Assistant.

clock_drift.title: {name}'s clock is {minutes} minutes {direction}
clock_drift.description:
The fireplace's own timers run on its clock, so they're switching it on and off {minutes} minutes off schedule. Set the time on the fireplace's remote or in the Escea app. If the clock keeps drifting, the fire may have lost power.

Timers in Home Assistant automations aren't affected.
